assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental markets and behavioural game theory made controlled evidence central to the study of strategic economic behaviour.
assessment.attribution: Holt, Plott and Camerer provide a coherent, highly influential core spanning market experiments, institutional testing and strategic behaviour.
assessment.maturity: The research programme is longstanding, widely used and tested across experimental economics.
uncertainties: The discovery label encompasses several related traditions, making a three-person allocation necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete choice supplied a practical framework for estimating forward-looking decisions and changed empirical work in many applied fields.
assessment.attribution: Rust is foundational, while Keane and Eckstein are central contributors to structural dynamic-choice estimation and applications.
assessment.maturity: Its methodological and empirical influence has accumulated over decades.
uncertainties: Structural estimates can depend materially on modeling and identification assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of reciprocity, fairness and inequity aversion substantially revised standard accounts of economic motivation and strategic interaction.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Schmidt supplied an especially identifiable theoretical core, with Falk a major experimental contributor to the broader programme.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have generated extensive experimental and applied evidence over a long period.
uncertainties: The breadth and context-dependence of social-preference evidence complicate a single canonical formulation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression enabled systematic analysis of heterogeneous and distributional relationships beyond conditional means.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett are the clear foundational pair; Chernozhukov represents major later development of distributional econometrics.
assessment.maturity: The method is durable, broadly deployed and supported by an extensive theoretical literature.
uncertainties: The contribution is a powerful general method, so its ultimate prize framing relative to other econometric advances is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection transformed modern trade theory and empirical interpretation of trade gains and adjustment.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the central originator of the canonical framework, with Helpman and Redding important contributors to its development and applications.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been deeply integrated into trade research and policy analysis.
uncertainties: Attribution overlaps with adjacent trade and firm-heterogeneity contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The combination of theory and measurement for adverse selection made insurance-market information problems empirically tractable and policy relevant.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav and Salanie form a credible complementary group connecting empirical identification, market design and theory.
assessment.maturity: The work has produced sustained evidence and has shaped health, credit and insurance economics.
uncertainties: Empirical diagnosis of selection and welfare effects can remain sensitive to institutional setting and model structure.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The reconstruction of long-run income and wealth distributions changed the empirical basis for studying inequality and taxation.
assessment.attribution: Piketty, Saez and Zucman constitute a recognizable core for linked work on top incomes, wealth and offshore holdings.
assessment.maturity: The programme has had major scholarly and public-policy influence and has developed over many years.
uncertainties: Historical and cross-border wealth estimates require consequential data construction and capitalization assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence on early-life conditions and skill formation established that health and human-capital shocks early in life have persistent economic consequences.
assessment.attribution: Currie and Almond are central empirical contributors, while Cunha provides an important dynamic skill-formation framework.
assessment.maturity: The evidence base is extensive and the findings have clear relevance for health, education and social policy.
uncertainties: Causal estimates and external validity can vary across cohorts, shocks and policy environments.
